content.target_topic: Independent open property discovery and candidate CBMC harness generation for ML-KEM polynomial addition

property_discovery.selection_reason: Selected after the LLM-authored candidate set was saved and post-classified. Selection is an experiment-control decision, not proof that the property is true.

raw_candidate_set.title: Fixed-bound traversal of all 256 coefficients
raw_candidate_set.candidate_statement: mlk_poly_add traverses exactly the coefficient indices 0 through MLKEM_N - 1, and with MLKEM_N = 256 this means one visit per coefficient with no early exit or secondary index.

supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The routine is a single bounded loop that touches one coefficient index per iteration.
The loop bound resolves to 256 iterations.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: An element f of R_q is a polynomial ... represented by the array (f0, f1, ..., f255) ∈ Z_q^256.
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The spec uses 256-entry coefficient arrays for the polynomial representation.

required_assumptions: MLKEM_N is 256 in the compiled snapshot.
The visible loop is the complete routine body for this target function.
out_of_scope_boundaries: Does not assert modular arithmetic semantics or coefficient-range preservation.
Does not decide aliasing policy or memory-safety preconditions.
raw_candidate_set.uncertainty: The bound is explicit and the body is simple, but the snapshot does not include any formal loop contract or harness.
limitations: This property is about traversal coverage only; it does not capture the arithmetic meaning of each assignment.

raw_candidate_set.title: Indexed destination update equals casted sum
raw_candidate_set.candidate_statement: For each index i, the post-state value stored in r->coeffs[i] is the int16_t cast of the sum of the pre-state destination coefficient r->coeffs[i] and the source coefficient b->coeffs[i] at the same index.

supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The code performs the exact per-index assignment described in the candidate statement.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: W ← X + Y will result in W[i] = X[i] + Y[i] for all i.
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The specification’s array-add semantics are coordinate-wise on matching indices.

required_assumptions: The proof records the pre-state value of r->coeffs[i] before each assignment.
The C narrowing conversion to int16_t is modeled explicitly in the checking context.
out_of_scope_boundaries: Does not claim modulo-q normalization or canonical residue preservation.
Does not claim anything about values outside the shown per-index assignment.
raw_candidate_set.uncertainty: The body shows a narrowing cast, so the exact stored-value interpretation depends on the verification model for C integer conversion.
limitations: A stronger modular-correctness statement is not implied by this local state transition alone.

raw_candidate_set.title: Write footprint confined to destination polynomial
raw_candidate_set.candidate_statement: The visible body writes only through r->coeffs[i]; no direct store targets b or any other storage in the shown function body.

supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The assignment writes through r only.
The interface distinguishes a mutable destination pointer from a const source pointer.

required_assumptions: The property is interpreted only over direct writes in the shown function body.
out_of_scope_boundaries: Does not rule out indirect effects on shared storage if r and b alias.
Does not assert that b's underlying object cannot change through aliasing with r.
raw_candidate_set.uncertainty: The source pointer is const-qualified, but the snapshot does not include an aliasing contract that would make a stronger separation claim.
limitations: This is a direct frame property only; it does not speak to arithmetic correctness.

raw_candidate_set.title: Valid-object precondition for both polynomial arguments
raw_candidate_set.candidate_statement: A safe invocation requires both r and b to designate accessible mlk_poly objects spanning all MLKEM_N coefficients, because the loop unconditionally dereferences both arrays.

supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The body dereferences both pointers repeatedly without runtime checks.
The expected object shape is a fixed-length coefficient array of int16_t values.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: Existing target-specific function contracts, loop contracts, proof harnesses, and comments disclosing formal assumptions are intentionally excluded from the LLM-visible experiment snapshot.
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: No explicit contract or harness is visible in the provided source snapshot.

required_assumptions: r is non-null and points to an accessible mlk_poly object.
b is non-null and points to an accessible mlk_poly object.
Each accessible object spans at least MLKEM_N int16_t coefficients.
out_of_scope_boundaries: Does not prove that the function establishes these preconditions itself.
Does not describe any caller-side ownership or lifetime policy.
raw_candidate_set.uncertainty: No runtime checks or visible contracts state how invalid inputs should be handled.
limitations: This is a caller-side safety obligation, not an implementation guarantee.

raw_candidate_set.title: Aliasing between destination and source is unspecified
raw_candidate_set.candidate_statement: The visible snapshot does not determine whether r and b may alias; because the same coefficient position is both read and written in each iteration, overlap behavior remains an explicit open relational case.

supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The interface itself does not state a no-alias or must-alias rule.
Each iteration reads and writes the same coefficient index, so overlap behavior matters.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: Existing target-specific function contracts, loop contracts, proof harnesses, and comments disclosing formal assumptions are intentionally excluded from the LLM-visible experiment snapshot.
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: A visible aliasing contract is not available in the provided snapshot.

required_assumptions: Any later proof that needs a separation policy must state an explicit alias assumption; the visible snapshot does not provide one.
out_of_scope_boundaries: Does not decide whether aliasing is intended, permitted, or forbidden.
Does not claim a correctness result under any specific alias model.
raw_candidate_set.uncertainty: The intended alias policy may exist in excluded contracts or surrounding code, but it is not visible here.
limitations: Any harness that silently assumes disjointness would be stronger than the provided evidence.

raw_candidate_set.title: Visible body lacks explicit mod-q normalization
raw_candidate_set.candidate_statement: The shown implementation computes plain integer addition followed by an int16_t cast, but it does not visibly perform reduction modulo MLKEM_Q; therefore a direct FIPS-style modular-add correspondence needs an extra invariant or omitted normalization step.

supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The shown code uses addition and a cast, with no explicit mod-q operation.
The implementation header defines the q context constant used for ML-KEM arithmetic.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: z ← x+y means that z is assigned the value x + y mod m.
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The specification defines assignment into Z_m as modular reduction.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: The algebraic operations of addition and scalar multiplication in R_q and T_q are done coordinate-wise.
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The specification’s polynomial and NTT addition semantics are coordinate-wise and modular.

required_assumptions: If the goal is FIPS-style modular equality, an external invariant or omitted normalization step must connect the raw C result to MLKEM_Q semantics.
The property is evaluated only against the shown body, not hidden repository code.
out_of_scope_boundaries: Does not assert the routine is incorrect; it only marks the modular-equivalence proof obligation as unsupported by the visible body alone.
Does not claim full ML-KEM correctness or compliance.
raw_candidate_set.uncertainty: The snapshot may omit surrounding invariants or post-processing that restore modular semantics, so the gap cannot be closed from this evidence alone.
limitations: This is a proof-obligation gap rather than a directly checkable local invariant.
